skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline

skills.name: coding-standards

skills.name: daemon-development

skills.name: gdb-debugging

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development
skills.description: Guide for developing, building, and running Nanvix user-space applications across supported runtimes and languages. Use this when asked about guest app implementation or execution.

# TCB Allowed List — Nanvix phys-mm

Any `external_body` outside this list must be removed.

## Allowed `external_body`

- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::instance` — materializes a `&'static mut Inner` from the
  module-level `static mut INSTANCE: MaybeUninit<Inner>` singleton (guarded by `INSTANCE_INIT`).
  Raw-memory op over externally-owned `static mut` storage Verus cannot verify without a
  `PointsTo` (mirrors `bump_allocator`/`raw-array`). `ensures` pins the singleton's abstract
  state to `phys_view().frames`, asserts `(*r).inv()`, and records `phys_view().initialized` —
  the §8 ghost-token attachment for the singleton frame allocator.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::deref`
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::deref_mut`
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::clear`
- `src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs::FixedSizeBumpAllocator::alloc` — materializes a
  `&'static mut [u8; N]` from a backend-provided address (`usize as *mut`); raw-memory
  op Verus cannot verify without a `PointsTo` for the externally-owned `BssStorage`
  region. Mirrors `src/libs/raw-array`. `ensures` states alignment + in-bounds over
  the abstract `bump_view`.
- `src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs::FixedSizeBumpAllocator::alloc_as` — delegates to
  `alloc` and re-materializes the slot as `&'static mut MaybeUninit<T>`; same rationale.
  `ensures` adds the `size_of::<T>()`/`align_of::<T>()` vs `(N, A)` guard arms.

## `external_body` introduced while speccing `arch::x86::mem::paging::table`

- `src/libs/arch/src/x86/mem/paging/table.rs::Table::<E>::read` — reads a `TableEntry` from a
  page-table slot through a raw pointer materialized from `self.base` (`usize as *const E::Word`).
  Verus does not support `usize`→pointer casts (int-to-ptr materialization of externally-owned,
  volatile page-table memory), so the body cannot be verified. Same trust-boundary rationale as
  `bump_allocator::alloc` (`usize as *mut`) and `frame::instance`. See
  `nanvix-phys-arch-paging-table/verus-unsupported.md`. **The function is not contract-free:** it
  carries a full `#[verus_spec]` pinned to the global page-table-memory ghost — `requires index@ <
  PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`, `ensures result == spec_table_read::<E>(self@.addr, index@)` — exactly as
  `frame::instance` pins its result to `phys_view()` (parameter-free global ghost, no signature
  change).
- `src/libs/arch/src/x86/mem/paging/table.rs::Table::<E>::write` — writes a `TableEntry` into a
  page-table slot through a raw pointer materialized from `self.base` (`usize as *mut E::Word`).
  Same int-to-ptr / volatile externally-owned-memory limitation as `read`. Carries only the sound
  `requires index@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH` (auto from `TableIndex::inv`); it has **no** contents
  `ensures`. A contents postcondition pinning the *pure* global ghost `spec_table_word(self@.addr,
  index@)` to the caller-chosen `entry` would be unsound for an `external_body` (assumed)
  contract: two writes of distinct entries to the same slot would assume
  `spec_entry_raw(e1) == spec_entry_raw(e2)`, which with `lemma_entry_roundtrip` derives
  `e1 == e2`, i.e. `false` (Turn 2 review #2/#3/#15; exploit reproduced). The genuine `old@ -> @`
  slot-update transition (`self@.entries[index@] == Some(entry)`, other slots framed) is therefore
  **deferred to the proving-phase page-table permission token**, exactly the `identity_map_view()`
  `v -> v'` deferral convention in `identity_map.spec.rs`.

## `external_body` introduced while speccing `arch::x86::mem::paging` (`mod.rs`)

- `src/libs/arch/src/x86/mem/paging/mod.rs::invlpg` — the body is a single
  `core::arch::asm!` block issuing the `invlpg` instruction, which flushes the CPU TLB
  entry for `vaddr`. Verus does not support inline-asm expressions, so the body cannot be
  verified — an external-bottom hardware trust boundary (same class as the volatile
  page-table access in `table::read`/`write` and the int-to-pointer materialization in
  `frame::instance`/`bump_allocator::alloc`). See
  `nanvix-phys-arch-paging-mod/verus-unsupported.md`. The effect is purely on hardware TLB
  state (outside Verus' memory model and invisible to every caller's Rust-visible state),
  so the faithful contract is **empty**: no `requires` (any `usize` is accepted), trivial
  `ensures` (returns `()`, no Rust-visible effect, every caller-side invariant preserved).
  This matches the inherited upstream
  `src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.spec.rs:151`
  `pub assume_specification[ ::arch::mem::paging::invlpg ](vaddr: usize);` (no
  `requires`/`ensures`). No exec signature changed.

## Skip / exclude from current proof target

- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs::PhysMemoryManager::get_mut`
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::init`

## `external_body` introduced while speccing `mm::phys`

- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/mod.rs::book_physical_memory_regions` — iterates an
  `alloc::collections::LinkedList` in a `for` loop. Verus has no `LinkedList` model and the
  orphan rule blocks providing one from the kernel crate (see
  `nanvix-phys-phys-mod/bugs.md`). Body cannot be verified; `ensures` states that, on `Ok`,
  every frame in `phys_regions_frame_set(&physical_memory_regions)` becomes reserved.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/mod.rs::book_mmio_regions` — same `LinkedList` limitation.
  `ensures` states that, on `Ok`, every *covered* frame in `mmio_regions_frame_set(mmio_regions)`
  becomes reserved (uncovered MMIO frames are skipped, matching the `frame::is_covered` gate).

## Cross-module dependencies marked `external_body` (eliminated when their module is verified)

- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::init` — also listed under skip; callable from verified `init`.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs::PhysMemoryManager::init` — no specs yet; opaque callee.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/upool.rs::Upool` (struct) and `Upool::new` — no specs yet; opaque
  type/callee needed so verified `init` can construct the user page pool.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/upool.rs::Upool::alloc` — pool allocation primitive the manager's user
  paths call. `ensures` describes the free→allocated transition (`alloc_one`) and the empty-pool
  `Err` arm (`free_count() == 0`). Verified when `upool` is.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::new` — wraps a `FrameAddress` into an owning
  kernel-frame handle. `ensures Ok(kf) => kf@ == base@`. Verified when `kframe` is.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::alloc` — singleton wrapper around `Inner::alloc`;
  `ensures Ok(frame) => frame.inv()`.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::alloc_contiguous` — singleton wrapper around
  `Inner::alloc_contiguous`; `requires count > 0`, `ensures` page-aligned base plus the
  address-space range bound the manager's index arithmetic relies upon.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::free_count` — reports the free-partition size
  (`== phys_view().frames.free_count()`).
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::free` — best-effort frame release used by manager error
  cleanup; no precondition, no abstract postcondition (callers ignore the outcome).
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::book` — singleton wrapper around `Inner::book`. Reserves a
  covered, previously-free frame so `alloc` never hands it out. `requires phys_addr.inv()`,
  `ensures Ok(()) => phys_view().frames.reserved(phys_addr@)`. The free→allocated transition
  lives in `Inner::book` (verified in-body); the wrapper's postcondition references the
  *post-mutation* `phys_view().frames`, which the parameter-free `phys_view()` accessor cannot
  express until the §8 ghost token is realized (`instance()` pins it to the *pre*-state). Same
  cross-module deferral as `frame::alloc`; `external_body` until the free-function layer is
  verified.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::alloc_range` — singleton wrapper around `Inner::alloc_range`.
  On success every (free) frame in the region is reserved. `requires region.inv()`,
  `ensures Ok(()) => phys_view().frames.all_reserved(region_frame_addrs(..))`. Same
  post-mutation `phys_view()` deferral as `frame::book`; `external_body` until the free-function
  layer is verified.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::share` — singleton wrapper around `Inner::share` (the CoW
  reference-count bump). `requires frame.inv()`, `ensures Ok(()) => the frame is allocated in
  `phys_view().frames``. The per-frame `+1` lives in the global partition and is pinned to
  `phys_view().frames` in the proving phase. Sibling of `frame::alloc`/`free`; `external_body`
  until the free-function layer is verified.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::refcount` — singleton wrapper around `Inner::refcount`.
  `requires frame.inv()`, `ensures Ok(count) => count == phys_view().frames.refcounts[frame@]`
  and `Err(_) => frame not allocated`. Pure read; `external_body` until the free-function layer
  is verified.
- `src/kernel/src/hal/mem/types/address/frame.rs::FrameAddress::from_raw_value` — succeeds only
  for page-aligned inputs, so `ensures Ok(fa) => fa.inv()`. Verified when the address layer is.
- `src/kernel/src/hal/mem/types/address/frame.rs::FrameAddress::into_raw_value` — the raw value is
  the abstract frame address (`ensures result as int == self@`). Verified when the address layer is.

# TCB Allowed List — Nanvix phys-mm

Any `external_body` outside this list must be removed.

## Allowed `external_body`

- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::instance` — materializes a `&'static mut Inner` from the
  module-level `static mut INSTANCE: MaybeUninit<Inner>` singleton (guarded by `INSTANCE_INIT`).
  Raw-memory op over externally-owned `static mut` storage Verus cannot verify without a
  `PointsTo` (mirrors `bump_allocator`/`raw-array`). `ensures` pins the singleton's abstract
  state to `phys_view().frames`, asserts `(*r).inv()`, and records `phys_view().initialized` —
  the §8 ghost-token attachment for the singleton frame allocator.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::deref`
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::deref_mut`
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::clear`
- `src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs::FixedSizeBumpAllocator::alloc` — materializes a
  `&'static mut [u8; N]` from a backend-provided address (`usize as *mut`); raw-memory
  op Verus cannot verify without a `PointsTo` for the externally-owned `BssStorage`
  region. Mirrors `src/libs/raw-array`. `ensures` states alignment + in-bounds over
  the abstract `bump_view`.
- `src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs::FixedSizeBumpAllocator::alloc_as` — delegates to
  `alloc` and re-materializes the slot as `&'static mut MaybeUninit<T>`; same rationale.
  `ensures` adds the `size_of::<T>()`/`align_of::<T>()` vs `(N, A)` guard arms.

## `external_body` introduced while speccing `arch::x86::mem::paging::table`

- `src/libs/arch/src/x86/mem/paging/table.rs::Table::<E>::read` — reads a `TableEntry` from a
  page-table slot through a raw pointer materialized from `self.base` (`usize as *const E::Word`).
  Verus does not support `usize`→pointer casts (int-to-ptr materialization of externally-owned,
  volatile page-table memory), so the body cannot be verified. Same trust-boundary rationale as
  `bump_allocator::alloc` (`usize as *mut`) and `frame::instance`. See
  `nanvix-phys-arch-paging-table/verus-unsupported.md`. **The function is not contract-free:** it
  carries a full `#[verus_spec]` pinned to the global page-table-memory ghost — `requires index@ <
  PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`, `ensures result == spec_table_read::<E>(self@.addr, index@)` — exactly as
  `frame::instance` pins its result to `phys_view()` (parameter-free global ghost, no signature
  change).
- `src/libs/arch/src/x86/mem/paging/table.rs::Table::<E>::write` — writes a `TableEntry` into a
  page-table slot through a raw pointer materialized from `self.base` (`usize as *mut E::Word`).
  Same int-to-ptr / volatile externally-owned-memory limitation as `read`. Carries only the sound
  `requires index@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH` (auto from `TableIndex::inv`); it has **no** contents
  `ensures`. A contents postcondition pinning the *pure* global ghost `spec_table_word(self@.addr,
  index@)` to the caller-chosen `entry` would be unsound for an `external_body` (assumed)
  contract: two writes of distinct entries to the same slot would assume
  `spec_entry_raw(e1) == spec_entry_raw(e2)`, which with `lemma_entry_roundtrip` derives
  `e1 == e2`, i.e. `false` (Turn 2 review #2/#3/#15; exploit reproduced). The genuine `old@ -> @`
  slot-update transition (`self@.entries[index@] == Some(entry)`, other slots framed) is therefore
  **deferred to the proving-phase page-table permission token**, exactly the `identity_map_view()`
  `v -> v'` deferral convention in `identity_map.spec.rs`.

## `external_body` introduced while speccing `arch::x86::mem::paging` (`mod.rs`)

- `src/libs/arch/src/x86/mem/paging/mod.rs::invlpg` — the body is a single
  `core::arch::asm!` block issuing the `invlpg` instruction, which flushes the CPU TLB
  entry for `vaddr`. Verus does not support inline-asm expressions, so the body cannot be
  verified — an external-bottom hardware trust boundary (same class as the volatile
  page-table access in `table::read`/`write` and the int-to-pointer materialization in
  `frame::instance`/`bump_allocator::alloc`). See
  `nanvix-phys-arch-paging-mod/verus-unsupported.md`. The effect is purely on hardware TLB
  state (outside Verus' memory model and invisible to every caller's Rust-visible state),
  so the faithful contract is **empty**: no `requires` (any `usize` is accepted), trivial
  `ensures` (returns `()`, no Rust-visible effect, every caller-side invariant preserved).
  This matches the inherited upstream
  `src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.spec.rs:151`
  `pub assume_specification[ ::arch::mem::paging::invlpg ](vaddr: usize);` (no
  `requires`/`ensures`). No exec signature changed.

- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs::PhysMemoryManager::get_mut`
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::init`

  `nanvix-phys-phys-mod/bugs.md`). Body cannot be verified; `ensures` states that, on `Ok`,

  `ensures Ok(frame) => frame.inv()`.

  `Inner::alloc_contiguous`; `requires count > 0`, `ensures` page-aligned base plus the

  verified.

  `phys_view().frames``. The per-frame `+1` lives in the global partition and is pinned to

  until the free-function layer is verified.

  `requires frame.inv()`, `ensures Ok(count) => count == phys_view().frames.refcounts[frame@]`
  and `Err(_) => frame not allocated`. Pure read; `external_body` until the free-function layer
  is verified.

  the abstract frame address (`ensures result as int == self@`). Verified when the address layer is.

## External-bottom: build-time constant accessor

- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs::kernel_watermark` — `external_body` accessor that returns
  the build-time constant `config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK`. This constant is generated by the

1. verus! {
2. 
3. use crate::hal::mem::spec_page_size;
4. use crate::mm::phys::FrameAllocView;
5. 
6. // `Result::and_then`: on `Ok`, the closure is applied to the payload (its precondition must hold);
7. // on `Err`, the error is forwarded unchanged. Mirrors `core`'s implementation. vstd ships no
8. // specification for it.
9. pub assume_specification<T, E, U, F: FnOnce(T) -> Result<U, E>>[ Result::<T, E>::and_then ](
10.     result: Result<T, E>,
11.     op: F,
12. ) -> (res: Result<U, E>)
13.     requires
14.         result is Ok ==> op.requires((result->Ok_0,)),
15.     ensures
16.         result is Err ==> res == Err::<U, E>(result->Err_0),
17.         result is Ok ==> op.ensures((result->Ok_0,), res),
18. ;
19. 
20. // `Result::inspect_err`: runs a side-effecting closure on the error (if any) and returns the
21. // receiver unchanged. The closure is used purely for its effects, so no abstract obligation is
22. // threaded. vstd ships no specification for it.
23. pub assume_specification<T, E, F: FnOnce(&E)>[ Result::<T, E>::inspect_err ](
24.     result: Result<T, E>,
25.     f: F,
26. ) -> (res: Result<T, E>)
27.     ensures
28.         res == result,
29. ;
30. 
31. // `Vec::capacity`: reports spare storage; opaque with respect to the abstract sequence. vstd
32. // ships no specification for it.
33. pub assume_specification<T, A: ::core::alloc::Allocator>[ Vec::<T, A>::capacity ](
34.     vec: &Vec<T, A>,
35. ) -> (c: usize)
36. ;
37. 
38. //==================================================================================================
39. // Build-time kernel watermark
40. //==================================================================================================
41. 
42. /// The kernel watermark: the number of physical frames the kernel always keeps free for itself.
43. ///
44. /// User allocations are gated by this threshold; kernel allocations bypass it. Mirrors the
45. /// build-time constant `config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK`, which is generated by the `config`
46. /// crate's `build.rs` (from `kernel_config.toml`) and therefore lives outside Verus's view.
47. /// The abstract value is fixed by the `external_body` accessor `kernel_watermark()`; this is an
48. /// external-bottom trust boundary (see `verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md`). Callers do not depend on
49. /// the concrete threshold — only on the fact that user allocations are gated by it.
50. pub uninterp spec fn spec_kernel_watermark() -> nat;
51. 
52. //==================================================================================================
53. // Allocation / watermark vocabulary (on the existing FrameAllocView)
54. //==================================================================================================
55. 
56. impl FrameAllocView {
57.     /// Number of frames currently free, i.e. available to hand out. This is the single quantity
58.     /// the kernel watermark reads. Models `frame::free_count()`.
59.     pub open spec fn free_count(self) -> nat {
60.         self.free_frames.len()
61.     }
62. 
63.     /// A user allocation of `count` frames is admissible: fulfilling it would still leave at
64.     /// least `KERNEL_WATERMARK` frames free for the kernel. This is the predicate behind the
65.     /// user-vs-kernel asymmetry that `check_user_watermark` enforces.
66.     pub open spec fn user_alloc_ok(self, count: nat) -> bool {
67.         self.free_count() >= count + spec_kernel_watermark()
68.     }
69. 
70.     /// Allocate a single currently-free frame `addr`: move it from `free_frames` to
71.     /// `allocated_frames` with refcount 1. (Equivalent to `book_all(set![addr])`.)
72.     pub open spec fn alloc_one(self, addr: int) -> FrameAllocView {
73.         FrameAllocView {
74.             allocated_frames: self.allocated_frames.insert(addr),
75.             free_frames: self.free_frames.remove(addr),
76.             refcounts: self.refcounts.insert(addr, 1int),
77.         }
78.     }
79. }
80. 
81. //==================================================================================================
82. // Manager view
83. //==================================================================================================
84. 
85. impl View for PhysMemoryManager {
86.     type V = FrameAllocView;
87. 
88.     /// The manager brokers the global physical-frame partition. Its abstract state is exactly
89.     /// that partition, realized here through the user page pool it owns; the attachment to the
90.     /// global frame allocator (`self@ == phys_view().frames`) is pinned in the proving phase.
91.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> FrameAllocView {
92.         self.upool@
93.     }
94. }
95. 
96. impl PhysMemoryManager {
97.     /// Well-formedness invariant: the brokered frame partition is well formed (free/allocated
98.     /// disjoint, page-aligned, refcount <-> allocated consistent, refcounts in 1..=255).
99.     ///
100.     /// Liveness is structural (a `&mut self` is only obtainable after `init` succeeded) and the
101.     /// watermark is a per-user-allocation gate, not an invariant — kernel allocations are
102.     /// designed to dip below it — so neither appears here.
103.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
104.         self@.wf()
105.     }
106. }
107. 
108. //==================================================================================================
109. // Handle-set helpers
110. //==================================================================================================
111. 
112. /// The set of physical frame addresses owned by a sequence of user-frame handles.
113. pub open spec fn user_addr_set(frames: Seq<UserFrame>) -> Set<int> {
114.     Set::new(|a: int| exists|i: int| 0 <= i < frames.len() && #[trigger] frames[i]@ == a)
115. }
116. 
117. /// The set of physical frame addresses owned by a sequence of kernel-frame handles.
118. pub open spec fn kernel_addr_set(frames: Seq<KernelFrame>) -> Set<int> {
119.     Set::new(|a: int| exists|i: int| 0 <= i < frames.len() && #[trigger] frames[i]@ == a)
120. }
121. 
122. /// The first `count` kernel-frame handles in `frames` occupy a physically contiguous, page-aligned
123. /// run: there is a page-aligned `base` such that handle `i` owns `base + i * page_size`. This is the
124. /// identity-map contiguity guarantee that kernel-stack callers (`alloc_kpages`) depend on.
125. pub open spec fn kernel_frames_contiguous(frames: Seq<KernelFrame>, count: nat) -> bool {
126.     exists|base: int|
127.         #![trigger crate::mm::phys::region_frame_addrs(base, (count * spec_page_size()) as int)]
128.         base % spec_page_size() == 0 && forall|i: int|
129.             0 <= i < count ==> #[trigger] frames[i]@ == base + i * spec_page_size()
130. }
131. 
132. } // verus!

---
name: verus-constraints
description: "Mandatory rules for writing Verus code. Covers verus! block syntax, source integrity for exec code, forbidden patterns, and assume_specification policy. Must be followed whenever producing or modifying Verus-annotated code."
---

# Verus Constraints

Study `docs/examples/binary-search/proof/` for a complete example following all
constraints below.

## verus! { } Blocks Only

All spec and proof code **must** use native `verus! { }` block syntax.
Do **not** use attribute-based syntax (`#[verus_spec]`, `#[verus_verify]`, `proof! { }`).

```rust
// ✅ CORRECT
verus! {
    fn foo(x: u32) -> (ret: u32)
        requires x < 100,
        ensures ret == x + 1,
    { x + 1 }
} // verus!

// ❌ WRONG — attribute style
#[verus_spec(ret => requires x < 100, ensures ret == x + 1)]
fn foo(x: u32) -> u32 { x + 1 }
```

Even if existing code uses attribute style, write all new code in `verus! { }` style.
Attribute style is less mature; `verus! { }` can be auto-converted later.

## Source Integrity (exec code)

The following rules apply to the original source files (e.g. `lib.rs`), not to
`*.spec.rs` / `*.proof.rs` which are freely editable.

Verus verification is **in-place**: specs and proofs are added directly alongside
exec code. The annotated code remains fully compilable and runnable — Verus
constructs are erased during normal `cargo build` via cfg-gating. Do not change
code logic; keep changes minimal so developers can review diffs easily.

**Preserve:** exec logic, function signatures, struct definitions, comments,
debug assertions, and all other existing code. If a construct is unsupported by
Verus (e.g. `debug_assert!`), cfg-gate it with `#[cfg(not(verus_keep_ghost))]`
rather than deleting.

**Allowed additions:** `verus! { }` blocks (requires, ensures, invariants, decreases,
proof blocks, assert), vstd imports (cfg-gated), named returns `-> (ret: T)`,
ghost/tracked variables, `#[cfg_attr(not(verus_keep_ghost), derive(...))]` gating.

**Never change:** semantic code logic or function/struct signatures. Exception:
only if Verus genuinely cannot express a construct — first search vstd for
alternatives, build a minimal reproducer proving unsupported, then make the
smallest change needed and document why.

**Iterator rewrite rule:** When exec code uses Iterator chains
(`.iter().filter().map().collect()`), these MUST be rewritten to while
loops because Iterator API is unsupported. This is a permitted exec
change because: (1) the behavioral semantics are identical, (2) it is
a true Verus limitation, (3) the ensures should describe the ORIGINAL
functional intent using `Seq::filter`/`Seq::map_values`, not the
rewritten loop structure.

**After completing all changes**, use the `ast-consistency` skill to verify
source integrity. Fix all inconsistencies. For unavoidable ones, you must
confirm: (1) the code still builds with `cargo build`, (2) semantic code logic
is unchanged, (3) it is a genuine Verus limitation, and (4) it is documented.

## Forbidden Patterns

| Pattern | Policy |
|---|---|
| `admit()` | Banned — only as placeholder in initial skeleton proofs |
| `assume(...)` | Banned |
| `#[verifier::external_body]` | Banned **as a workaround** for spec/proof difficulty. Permitted ONLY for functions that use a True Limitation feature (async, float arithmetic, transmute, static mut) — see True Limitations table below. If the function body is pure Rust with supported types, it MUST be verified, not escaped. |
| `#[verifier::trusted]` | Banned |
| `#[verifier::external]` | Banned — do not use to "fix" verification errors |
| `#[verifier::exec_allows_no_decreases_clause]` | Banned |
| `#[verifier::rlimit(N)]` | Timeout means the proof is too weak — simplify the proof, split lemmas, add intermediate assertions. Never use rlimit to work around timeouts. If all proof strategies are exhausted and the proof is genuinely optimal, rlimit up to 50 is the absolute maximum |

## assume_specification — Human-Approved Only

`assume_specification` and `axiom` are **external-bottom** trust
assumptions (see **spec-design** skill, Part 2). They introduce
unverified axioms — if wrong, the entire verification is unsound.

`external_type_specification` is safe to use freely — it only declares
that a type exists without introducing logical assumptions.

**You must NOT write `assume_specification` or `axiom` yourself** unless
a human has explicitly approved them (e.g., via checked items in the
property analysis). If you discover a missing assumption, report it and
use `admit()` as a temporary placeholder.

**Before reporting:** search vstd for existing specs of that function,
look for safe Verus API alternatives, try restructuring to avoid the call.

## vstd & Common Misconceptions

Before writing custom specs, search vstd for existing ones (sequences, sets,
maps, arithmetic, pointers, atomics).

- **Never invent vstd functions** — verify existence in actual vstd source.
- **Verus supports `for` loops** — do not replace with `while` unless semantically appropriate.
- **Don't hallucinate syntax** — when unsure, check the Verus reference or vstd examples.

## False Limitations (v0.2026.04.03)

The following features **work** in current Verus. Do NOT claim they are unsupported:

| Feature | Status | Notes |
|---------|--------|-------|
| `dyn trait` (basic + Box\<dyn\>) | ✅ Works | Including trait with spec methods |
| `DerefMut` / `v[i] = x` on `&mut Vec` | ✅ Works | Use `v.set(i, x)` |
| Multiple `&mut` params (`swap(a, b)`) | ✅ Works | `old(a)`, `old(b)` in ensures |
| `std::collections::HashMap` (basic) | ✅ Works | `new()`, `insert()` verified |
| `Box::new` with ensures | ✅ Works | `ensures *b == 42` |
| `Option::unwrap_or` | ✅ Works | |
| Nested `proof fn` calls (3+ layers) | ✅ Works | |
| `for` loop with `iter:` | ✅ Works | |
| `const fn` | ✅ Works | Needs overflow handling |
| Recursive types (`Box<Self>`) | ✅ Works | Add `decreases self` |
| `type_invariant` | ✅ Works | Use `proof { use_type_invariant(self); }` |
| `broadcast proof/use` | ✅ Works | |
| `Seq::filter` / `Seq::map_values` in spec | ✅ Works | Exec needs loop, but spec can use these |

## Spec Vocabulary Reference

When writing spec, you have these tools. Each includes **when to use** (not just what it is):

**choose:** `choose|x: T| P(x)` — Use when you have `exists|x| P(x)` and need a concrete witness value in a spec expression. Without this, you cannot define spec functions that "pick" a satisfying element.

**Extensional equality:** `=~=` for Seq/Set/Map, `=~~=` for nested collections. In many simple cases `==` also works for Seq, but when Z3 struggles with collection equality, switch to `=~=`. **Guideline: start with `==`, use `=~=` if Z3 can't prove it.**

**old():** `old(self)@` in ensures of `&mut` functions. **Test: does this function take &mut? Then ensures MUST contain old().** Without this, ensures compares new state to itself (tautological).

**ghost struct:** Use when you need a spec-only abstraction that has no exec counterpart. Example: an `Interval { lo: int, hi: int }` for reasoning about address ranges that don't exist as a runtime type.

**spec_fn:** `spec_fn(T) -> U` — Use when a spec needs to be parameterized by a function. Example: a generic "map" spec that takes a transformation function.

**Seq operations in spec:** Even though `Iterator` chains are not available in exec, `Seq` provides the same operations in spec: `s.filter(|x| p(x))`, `s.map_values(|x| f(x))`, `s.subrange(lo, hi)`, `s.update(i, x)`, `s.contains(x)`. **When exec uses a while loop to implement filter/map, the ensures should still use Seq::filter/map_values to express the intent declaratively.**

**Map::dom():** Returns `Set<K>`. Use for "all keys satisfy P": `forall|k| m.dom().contains(k) ==> P(m[k])`. Without this, you can't quantify over Map keys.

## True Limitations (cannot work around in spec)

| Feature | Impact on Spec |
|---------|---------------|
| `async fn` / `await` | Cannot write requires/ensures. Must use `#[verifier::external]`. |
| `f32`/`f64` arithmetic in spec | Cannot reason about float results. |
| `static mut` | No spec model. |
| `transmute` | No spec model. |

# Bugs — Nanvix phys manager

## Observations (record-only; validated in the proving phase)

### OBS-1: `alloc_many_kernel_frames` lacks the `count == 0` fast-path guard

`alloc_many_user_frames` early-returns `Ok(())` when `count == 0`, but
`alloc_many_kernel_frames` has no such guard and unconditionally calls
`frame::alloc_contiguous(count)`. `Inner::alloc_contiguous` (and therefore the
`frame::alloc_contiguous` wrapper) `requires count > 0`, so a `count == 0` call
would violate that precondition.

- **Spec decision**: added `requires count > 0` to
  `PhysMemoryManager::alloc_many_kernel_frames`, matching the contiguous
  allocator it delegates to. The sole caller (`mm::virt::manager::alloc_kpages`,
  not yet verified) must establish `count > 0`; this becomes an obligation when
  that module is verified.
- **Not auto-fixed**: adding a `count == 0` early return would change exec
  behavior of an unverified caller path. Recorded for the proving phase to
  decide whether to add the guard (code fix) or keep the precondition.

### OBS-2: `alloc_many_user_frames` distinctness depends on allocator non-aliasing

The Ok-arm contract now asserts `user_addr_set(frames@).len() == count` — the
`count` returned handles own *distinct* physical frames. This is the property
that closes the duplicate-frame / double-free hazard: without it, two handles in
`frames` could alias the same address, so `book_all` would reserve fewer than
`count` frames while the caller believes it owns `count`, and dropping both would
free the same frame twice.

- **Spec decision**: added `user_addr_set(final(frames)@).len() == count` to the
  Ok arm of `alloc_many_user_frames`, and strengthened `lemma_user_bulk_ok`'s
  `ensures` with `user_addr_set(frames).len() == count` (body still `admit()`).
- **Proving-phase obligation**: distinctness must be discharged from the frame
  allocator's non-aliasing guarantee — each successful `frame::alloc` returns an
  address not currently in `free_frames`/`allocated_frames` overlap and removes
  it, so the per-iteration `push`ed addresses are pairwise distinct. This relies
  on `frame::alloc`'s (not-yet-verified) postcondition that the returned frame
  was free and becomes reserved. Recorded; no code change required.

would violate that precondition.

  allocator it delegates to. The sole caller (`mm::virt::manager::alloc_kpages`,
  not yet verified) must establish `count > 0`; this becomes an obligation when

  behavior of an unverified caller path. Recorded for the proving phase to
  decide whether to add the guard (code fix) or keep the precondition.

`count` returned handles own *distinct* physical frames. This is the property
that closes the duplicate-frame / double-free hazard: without it, two handles in
`frames` could alias the same address, so `book_all` would reserve fewer than
`count` frames while the caller believes it owns `count`, and dropping both would
free the same frame twice.

  Ok arm of `alloc_many_user_frames`, and strengthened `lemma_user_bulk_ok`'s
  `ensures` with `user_addr_set(frames).len() == count` (body still `admit()`).

  allocator's non-aliasing guarantee — each successful `frame::alloc` returns an
  address not currently in `free_frames`/`allocated_frames` overlap and removes
  it, so the per-iteration `push`ed addresses are pairwise distinct. This relies
  on `frame::alloc`'s (not-yet-verified) postcondition that the returned frame
  was free and becomes reserved. Recorded; no code change required.

soundness landmine callable from any proof.

name: ast-consistency
description: "AST-level exec fidelity checking tools and pre-approved deviations. Use after modifying source files to verify exec code is unchanged."
---

# AST Consistency Check

Source exec code must not change during verification — see `verus-constraints`
for the full rules. This skill covers the **tooling** to enforce that guarantee.

## Tools

The checker uses tree-sitter to hash exec code after stripping all
ghost/proof/spec annotations. It detects changes invisible to textual diff.

`scripts/ast_consistency.py` provides four subcommands:
- `count` — quick pass/fail
- `summary` — per-element status table
- `diff --name "Fn::name"` — unified diff for one function/struct
- `report -o <dir>` — full report with all diffs

The `source` argument is optional. Use `--base-ref` to extract the original
from git, or omit both on `verus-ai/*` branches for auto-detection:

```bash
# Explicit original file:
python3 scripts/ast_consistency.py original.rs verified.rs count

# Via git ref:
python3 scripts/ast_consistency.py --base-ref main verified.rs count

# Auto-detect on verus-ai/* branches:
python3 scripts/ast_consistency.py verified.rs count
```

`diff` with `--full` shows specs; default is exec-only.

**MCP alternative**: If the `verus-ast` MCP server is registered, the same
functionality is available as tools (`ast_count`, `ast_summary`, `ast_diff`,
`ast_report`) with the same auto-detection.

## Pre-Approved Deviations

These minimal exec changes are known Verus limitations — no full deviation
process needed, but still document with a comment:

| Original | Verus Version | Reason |
|----------|--------------|--------|
| `self.x += 1` | `self.x = self.x + 1` | Compound assignment unsupported |
| `self.arr[i] \|= v` | `self.arr.set(i, self.arr[i] \| v)` | Mutable index unsupported |
| `-> T` | `-> (ret: T)` | Named returns for ensures |
| `#[derive(Clone, ...)]` | `#[cfg(not(verus_keep_ghost))] #[derive(...)]` | cfg-gating incompatible derives |
| `Ok(Self { .. })` | `let result = Self { .. }; Ok(result)` | Ensures needs to reference return value |
| `f(complex_expr)` | `let x = complex_expr; f(x)` | Intermediate value for assertions |
| `.ok_or_else(\|\| ...)` | `match ... { Some(v) => v, None => return Err(...) }` | Closures unsupported in some contexts |

## Handling MISMATCHes

When the checker reports a MISMATCH:

1. **Default: restore original code.** Exec changes are violations. Use
   `git show <base_ref>:path/to/file.rs` to view the original, then
   manually restore the changed exec code while keeping your annotations.
   Adapt the proof to the original code — not the other way around.
2. **Check pre-approved deviations.** If the change matches one above,
   keep it but add a comment documenting which deviation and why.
3. **Verify it's a real Verus limitation.** Before accepting any other
   change, confirm Verus genuinely cannot handle the original construct:
   - Search vstd for existing support (e.g. `checked_mul` has vstd specs)
   - Try alternative proof strategies that preserve the original code
   - Build a minimal reproducer proving the limitation
4. **If confirmed, document with full justification.** Add a `VERUS DEVIATION`
   comment explaining: what was changed, why the original doesn't work,
   what alternatives were tried, and why this is the smallest possible change.

---
name: ast-consistency
description: "AST-level exec fidelity checking tools and pre-approved deviations. Use after modifying source files to verify exec code is unchanged."
---

# AST Consistency Check

Source exec code must not change during verification — see `verus-constraints`
for the full rules. This skill covers the **tooling** to enforce that guarantee.

## Tools

The checker uses tree-sitter to hash exec code after stripping all
ghost/proof/spec annotations. It detects changes invisible to textual diff.

`scripts/ast_consistency.py` provides four subcommands:
- `count` — quick pass/fail
- `summary` — per-element status table
- `diff --name "Fn::name"` — unified diff for one function/struct
- `report -o <dir>` — full report with all diffs

The `source` argument is optional. Use `--base-ref` to extract the original
from git, or omit both on `verus-ai/*` branches for auto-detection:

```bash
# Explicit original file:
python3 scripts/ast_consistency.py original.rs verified.rs count

# Via git ref:
python3 scripts/ast_consistency.py --base-ref main verified.rs count

# Auto-detect on verus-ai/* branches:
python3 scripts/ast_consistency.py verified.rs count
```

`diff` with `--full` shows specs; default is exec-only.

**MCP alternative**: If the `verus-ast` MCP server is registered, the same
functionality is available as tools (`ast_count`, `ast_summary`, `ast_diff`,
`ast_report`) with the same auto-detection.

## Pre-Approved Deviations

These minimal exec changes are known Verus limitations — no full deviation
process needed, but still document with a comment:

| Original | Verus Version | Reason |
|----------|--------------|--------|
| `self.x += 1` | `self.x = self.x + 1` | Compound assignment unsupported |
| `self.arr[i] \|= v` | `self.arr.set(i, self.arr[i] \| v)` | Mutable index unsupported |
| `-> T` | `-> (ret: T)` | Named returns for ensures |
| `#[derive(Clone, ...)]` | `#[cfg(not(verus_keep_ghost))] #[derive(...)]` | cfg-gating incompatible derives |
| `Ok(Self { .. })` | `let result = Self { .. }; Ok(result)` | Ensures needs to reference return value |
| `f(complex_expr)` | `let x = complex_expr; f(x)` | Intermediate value for assertions |
| `.ok_or_else(\|\| ...)` | `match ... { Some(v) => v, None => return Err(...) }` | Closures unsupported in some contexts |

## Handling MISMATCHes

When the checker reports a MISMATCH:

1. **Default: restore original code.** Exec changes are violations. Use
   `git show <base_ref>:path/to/file.rs` to view the original, then
   manually restore the changed exec code while keeping your annotations.
   Adapt the proof to the original code — not the other way around.
2. **Check pre-approved deviations.** If the change matches one above,
   keep it but add a comment documenting which deviation and why.
3. **Verify it's a real Verus limitation.** Before accepting any other
   change, confirm Verus genuinely cannot handle the original construct:
   - Search vstd for existing support (e.g. `checked_mul` has vstd specs)
   - Try alternative proof strategies that preserve the original code
   - Build a minimal reproducer proving the limitation
4. **If confirmed, document with full justification.** Add a `VERUS DEVIATION`
   comment explaining: what was changed, why the original doesn't work,
   what alternatives were tried, and why this is the smallest possible change.

18. /// together with a per-frame reference count that models shared
19. /// ownership (e.g. copy-on-write after `share()`).

21. {
22.     pub allocated_frames: Set<int>,
23.     pub free_frames: Set<int>,

25.     /// A frame is present in the map iff it is currently allocated.

33.         // Page-alignment
34.         &&& forall|addr: int| self.allocated_frames.contains(addr) ==> addr % spec_page_size() == 0

38.         // Allocated ↔ refcount consistency: a frame is allocated iff it has a positive refcount
39.         &&& forall|addr: int| #[trigger] self.allocated_frames.contains(addr) <==>
40.             self.refcounts.contains_key(addr) && self.refcounts[addr] > 0
41.         // Free frames have no refcount entry
42.         &&& forall|addr: int| #[trigger] self.free_frames.contains(addr) ==>
43.             !self.refcounts.contains_key(addr)
44.         // Refcount bounded by u8 range
45.         &&& forall|addr: int| self.refcounts.contains_key(addr) ==>
46.             0 < self.refcounts[addr] <= 255

106.         &&& self.manager_ready ==> self.initialized
107.     }

123.     /// allocator knows about, allocated or free. Models `frame::is_covered`.
124.     pub open spec fn covers(self, addr: int) -> bool {
125.         self.allocated_frames.contains(addr) || self.free_frames.contains(addr)
126.     }

129.     /// never return it. This is the core caller-visible fact a "booked" frame satisfies.
130.     pub open spec fn reserved(self, addr: int) -> bool {
131.         self.allocated_frames.contains(addr)
132.     }
133. 
134.     /// Every frame address in `set` is reserved.
135.     pub open spec fn all_reserved(self, set: Set<int>) -> bool {
136.         forall|a: int| set.contains(a) ==> self.reserved(a)
137.     }
138.

140.     /// booked only if it is entirely free).
141.     pub open spec fn all_free(self, set: Set<int>) -> bool {
142.         forall|a: int| #[trigger] set.contains(a) ==> self.free_frames.contains(a)
143.     }
144. 
145.     /// Reserve every frame in `set` (each assumed free in `self`): move it from
146.     /// `free_frames` to `allocated_frames` with refcount 1.
147.     pub open spec fn book_all(self, set: Set<int>) -> FrameAllocView {
148.         FrameAllocView {

150.             free_frames: self.free_frames.difference(set),
151.             refcounts: self.refcounts.union_prefer_right(

153.             ),
154.         }
155.     }

158.     /// the MMIO booking rule.

# Verification TODO — phys-manager (cheating-elimination)

Honest hand-off of the proof gaps that could **not** be discharged within the
`kernel::mm::phys::manager` editable scope (`manager.rs`, `manager.spec.rs`,
`manager.proof.rs`). Recording here does **not** make the phase pass: each
remaining `admit()` still trips the cheating gate, so the phase result is
**BLOCKER**.

All four are the **same root cause**: the §8 global ghost-token attachment is
realized in the `frame` free-function layer, which is **out of scope** and
itself **still unverified** (`frame.rs` carries 8 `admit()`s — `alloc`,
`alloc_contiguous`, `free`, `share`, `refcount`, `book`, `is_covered`,
`alloc_range`). Until that layer is verified and exposes a tracked
partition-token, the manager cannot link its abstract view `self@`
(`= self.upool@`, a `closed` view over the `external_body` opaque `Upool`) to
the global `phys_view().frames`, nor express the pre→post transition of a
free-function allocator.

Evidence: removing all four `admit()`s and re-running
`make verify-kernel MODULE=mm::phys` yields exactly four
`postcondition not satisfied` errors at the lemma seams
(`38 verified, 4 errors`), with no collateral. Restoring them returns the tree
to `42 verified, 0 errors`.

---

## 1. `lemma_manager_attached` — `manager.proof.rs:12`

- **Postcondition that fails:** `m@ == phys_view().frames` (`manager.proof.rs:14`).
- **Verus error:** `error: postcondition not satisfied --> manager.proof.rs:14:9`.
- **Why blocked:** `m@` reduces to `m.upool@`. `Upool` is `external_body`
  (`upool.rs:221`, TCB-listed) with no spec-readable state, so `m.upool@` is
  opaque; `phys_view()` is a parameter-free `uninterp` constant
  (`mod.spec.rs:98`, a **DO-NOT-MODIFY** global view). No contract in the
  manager's editable scope links the two — the link is the singleton ghost
  token over `frame::INSTANCE` / the `PhysMemoryManager` singleton, owned by the
  out-of-scope `frame` layer.
- **Unblock prerequisite:** verify `frame.rs` and have `frame::instance()` /
  `Upool` expose a tracked token whose value is `phys_view().frames`; then this
  lemma becomes `token.value() == self.upool@` by the token invariant.

## 2. `lemma_kernel_alloc_one` — `manager.proof.rs:27`

- **Postconditions that fail:** `pre.free_frames.contains(addr)` and
  `post == pre.alloc_one(addr)` (`manager.proof.rs:31-32`).
- **Verus error:** `error: postcondition not satisfied --> manager.proof.rs:31:9`
  and `:32:9`.
- **Why blocked:** the caller `alloc_kernel_frame` obtains its frame from
  `frame::alloc()` — a **free function** (`frame.rs:769`) that takes no `self`.
  In the Verus exec model `self` is untouched across the call, so the only
  provable fact is `final(self)@ == old(self)@`, while the spec demands the
  transition `final(self)@ == old(self)@.alloc_one(addr)`. `frame::alloc`'s
  contract can only reference the parameter-free constant `phys_view().frames`
  (it cannot express a `v -> v'` step). Contrast the **user** path, which is
  fully proven precisely because `Upool::alloc` takes `&mut self`
  (`upool.rs:279`, `final@ == old@.alloc_one(uf@)`) and threads the transition.
- **Unblock prerequisite:** a versioned/stepped tracked token threaded through
  `frame::alloc` (signature change to the out-of-scope `frame` layer) so the
  free→reserved step is expressible.

## 3. `lemma_kernel_alloc_contiguous` — `manager.proof.rs:40`

- **Postconditions that fail:** `frames.len() == count`,
  `kernel_frames_contiguous(frames, count)`,
  `post == pre.book_all(kernel_addr_set(frames))`,
  `pre.all_free(kernel_addr_set(frames))` (`manager.proof.rs:49-52`).
- **Verus error:** `error: postcondition not satisfied --> manager.proof.rs:49:9`
  and `:50:9`.
- **Why blocked:** identical to #2 but for the contiguous bulk path.
  `frame::alloc_contiguous` (`frame.rs:799`) is a free function returning only a
  base address plus a range bound; the per-frame free→reserved transition over
  the global partition is inexpressible without the stepped token.
- **Unblock prerequisite:** same as #2.

## 4. `lemma_user_bulk_err_restored` — `manager.proof.rs:210`

- **Postcondition that fails:** `m@ == pre` (`manager.proof.rs:214`).
- **Verus error:** `error: postcondition not satisfied --> manager.proof.rs:214:9`.
- **Why blocked:** on a mid-bulk failure `alloc_many_user_frames` calls
  `frames.clear()`, which **drops** the already-allocated `UserFrame`s; their
  `Drop` calls `frame::free` to return the frames, restoring the partition.
  Verus does **not** model `Drop` side effects, and `frame::free` is a free
  function that does not touch `self.upool@`, so after the proven loop
  transitions `self.upool@ == g_old.book_all(...)` and the model cannot reduce it
  back to `pre`. This is a genuine Drop-semantics + free-function gap.
- **Unblock prerequisite:** model the `UserFrame::drop` → `frame::free` release
  on the tracked partition token (again rooted in the out-of-scope `frame`
  layer), or an exec redesign that releases frames through a `&mut`-threaded
  method instead of `Drop` (out of scope — would change exec behavior).

---

## Sequencing recommendation

Verify the `frame` free-function layer (`nanvix-phys-phys-frame`) **first** so
it exposes a tracked global partition token. All four manager admits then
discharge mechanically:

- #1 from the token's value invariant,
- #2/#3 from the token's `alloc`/`alloc_contiguous` step lemmas,
- #4 from the token's `free` step applied per dropped handle.

No spec was weakened and no `external_body`/`assume` was introduced to mask
these gaps.

# Cheating Elimination Report: phys-manager

## Cheating Counts (before → after)

Scope: the manager module's editable files only — `manager.rs`,
`manager.spec.rs`, `manager.proof.rs`.

| Item | Before | After | Eliminated |
|------|--------|-------|------------|
| admit() | 4 | 4 | 0 |
| assume() | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| external_body | 2 | 2 | 0 (both TCB-allowed) |
| assume_specification | 3 | 3 | 0 (trusted std specs; gate-neutral) |
| cfg-gated exec | 9 | 9 | 0 (pre-approved logging gates) |

`make verify-kernel MODULE=mm::phys` → **42 verified, 0 errors** (unchanged
baseline). Full-crate `make verify` → all targets **exit 0** (cached, no
regressions). The cheating gate still reports `CHEATING_DETECTED` because of the
4 residual `admit()`s.

## Items Eliminated

None could be soundly eliminated within the manager's editable scope. The
escalation ladder (search vstd → isolated reproducer → equivalent rewrite) was
followed for each `admit()`; all four are the **same root cause** — the §8
global ghost-token attachment, which is realized in the out-of-scope, still
**unverified** `frame` free-function layer (`frame.rs` carries 8 of its own
`admit()`s). Concrete reproducer: removing all four `admit()`s and re-running
`make verify-kernel MODULE=mm::phys` produces exactly four
`postcondition not satisfied` errors at the lemma seams (`38 verified, 4
errors`) with no collateral; restoring them returns to `42 verified, 0 errors`.

`external_body` (`init`, `kernel_watermark`) are explicitly on
`verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md` (singleton `static mut` write; build-time
`config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK` constant from a non-Verus crate) — allowed,
not blockers. The three `assume_specification`s (`Result::and_then`,
`Result::inspect_err`, `Vec::capacity`) are trusted std-library contracts vstd
does not ship; they are not flagged by the cheating gate (`assume=0`) and were
established in the specification phase. The 9 cfg-gated exec lines guard
`error!`/`warn!` logging macros (unsupported constant type under Verus) — a
codebase-wide pre-approved deviation.

## Verification TODOs (verus-ai-logs/nanvix-phys-phys-manager/verification_todo.md)

All four are genuinely stuck on the out-of-scope `frame` layer's ghost token:

- **`lemma_manager_attached`** (`manager.proof.rs:12`) — `m@ == phys_view().frames`
  fails (`postcondition not satisfied @ :14:9`). `m@ = m.upool@` is opaque
  (`Upool` is `external_body`); `phys_view()` is a parameter-free `uninterp`
  DO-NOT-MODIFY constant. No in-scope contract links them.
- **`lemma_kernel_alloc_one`** (`manager.proof.rs:27`) —
  `post == pre.alloc_one(addr)` fails (`:31:9`, `:32:9`). Source obtains the
  frame from the free function `frame::alloc()` (no `self`), so Verus proves
  `final(self)@ == old(self)@`, not the demanded transition. (The user path is
  fully proven because `Upool::alloc` is `&mut self`.)
- **`lemma_kernel_alloc_contiguous`** (`manager.proof.rs:40`) — same as above for
  the contiguous bulk path via free function `frame::alloc_contiguous` (`:49:9`,
  `:50:9`).
- **`lemma_user_bulk_err_restored`** (`manager.proof.rs:210`) — `m@ == pre` fails
  (`:214:9`). On error `frames.clear()` relies on `UserFrame::drop → frame::free`;
  Verus does not model `Drop` side effects and `frame::free` is a free function,
  so `self.upool@` cannot be reduced back to `pre`.

**Unblock prerequisite (all four):** verify the `frame` free-function layer first
so it exposes a tracked global partition token; the four lemmas then discharge
mechanically (value invariant / step lemmas / per-handle free). No spec was
weakened and no new `external_body`/`assume` was introduced.

## AST Consistency

- `python3 ast_consistency.py --base-ref verus-ai-prove manager.rs summary` →
  `Consistent: ✅ YES (matched=8 mismatched=0 missing=0 extra=0)`.
- Source files are byte-identical to the phase-start commit
  (`git diff a8d643993 -- manager.rs manager.spec.rs manager.proof.rs` is empty).
- Zero mismatches confirmed: **YES**

## Result: BLOCKER

Four `admit()`s remain in `manager.proof.rs`. They are genuine §8 ghost-token /
`Drop`-model proof gaps whose discharge requires verifying and token-instrumenting
the out-of-scope `frame` free-function layer (itself still 8 `admit()`s). They
cannot be eliminated within the manager module's editable scope without either an
unsound axiom (banned) or an out-of-scope exec-signature change to `frame.rs`.
Recorded honestly in `verification_todo.md` with reproducers; the cheating gate
therefore remains tripped.

- `lemma_user_bulk_err_restored` — relies on `Drop → frame::free`, which Verus doesn't model.

Eliminating them requires verifying/token-instrumenting `frame.rs` (out of scope) or an unsound axiom (banned).
